name: Creekside Flats
award: 2024 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Archway Communities is building Creekside Flats, 150 income-restricted one- to three-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 80% AMI next to RTD's Sheridan light rail station in west Denver's Villa Park, replacing the 62-unit Jody Apartments on Urban Land Conservancy land trust ground; it won 2024 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits with $34M of CHFA bonds and broke ground in 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows a TOD redevelopment that more than doubles an expiring HOME-funded property on community land trust ground, using bond cap from Jefferson County, a $7.5M Denver linkage-fee loan and a 60-year city covenant.

status.label: Under construction (groundbreaking 2026); first residents expected 2027
status.detail: Denver's housing department announced the groundbreaking on 2026-06-11 and Archway posted it on 2026-07-08, with first residents expected in 2027. City Council approved the $7.5M city loan and a right-of-way encroachment permit on 2026-03-09. Financing closing is inferred from the groundbreaking; no closing date was published.

next_step: Watch for Denver building inspection milestones under project 2023-PROJMSTR-0000144 and lease-up notices in 2027.

key_numbers.meaning: 65 one-bedroom, 61 two-bedroom and 24 three-bedroom units at 30% to 80% AMI, with 22 units at 30% AMI.
About $29.9M over 10 years, plus $1,800,000 of accelerated state credit.
CHFA is the issuer; the city says Jefferson County contributed $10 million of its bond cap. The application planned $22.75M of permanent bonds and a taxable construction loan of about $14.08M.
Linkage-fee loan at 1% simple interest, 30-year term, with a 60-year affordability covenant.

facts.value: 5375 W. 10th Avenue, Denver 80214 (Villa Park), less than a quarter mile from Sheridan Station; the site sits on the Denver-Lakewood line by Dry Gulch (inferred from the city civil exhibit)
Four stories, wood frame, tuck-under parking, two stairs and two elevators; electrification-ready with photovoltaic arrays; trauma-informed design
C-MX-8; Denver planning confirmed the use and density are allowed with administrative approvals only, per the application
Land owned by ULC CLT, LLC (Urban Land Conservancy community land trust) since 2007; the project owner is the ground lessee
Creekside LLLP, whose general partner Creekside GP LLC is controlled by Archway Investment Corporation
Denver Housing Authority to join as special limited partner for property tax exemption, per the application
All units visitable; 16 homes fully accessible for mobility and 8 for sensory impairments
Partnership with Urban Peak for up to 10 units for youth exiting homelessness; Ardent Grove mental health services, Jovie childcare, food pantry, RTD EcoPasses

money.source: Colorado accelerated state housing tax credit
money.note: The applicant said state credits were necessary for feasibility.

CHFA is the issuer; privately placed construction bonds, $22,753,000 permanent bonds and a taxable construction loan of about $14,078,200, per the application. Jefferson County contributed $10 million of private activity bond cap through a partnership with Denver.

money.source: City and County of Denver loan (linkage fee)
money.note: Loan to Archway Investment Corporation, re-lent to Creekside LLLP; 1% simple interest, 360-month maturity; council resolution 26-0178 adopted 2026-03-09; closing deadline 2026-12-08; 60-year covenant.

money.source: Other sources named in the application
money.note: An FHLB grant, deferred developer fee, and a request for HUD Community Project Funding recommended by Senators Bennet and Hickenlooper; no award amounts were found. Archway also credits State of Colorado support.

parties.name: Creekside LLLP (general partner Creekside GP LLC)
Calcon (2024 estimate; final general contractor not confirmed)

background.text: Sheridan Homes, LLC (c/o NEWSED) bought a leasehold interest in the Jody Apartments in 2007 with a Denver HOME loan ($750,000, later raised to $923,100), while the land was deeded to ULC CLT, LLC; a 40-year affordability covenant was recorded on 2008-01-03 and ran to 2048.

On or about 2023-07-27 Sheridan repaid the city loan and sold the improvements to Archway Jody Acquisition LLC; City Council approved the assignment on 2024-01-16 (resolution 23-1673), tolling the remaining covenant term from 2023-07-27 until a final certificate of occupancy for the redevelopment. The sale price was not found.

The old building had 62 units; Archway relocated all 50 remaining households under the federal Uniform Relocation Act (completed November 2023), finished asbestos abatement in June 2024 and then demolished it.
A CDPHE Voluntary Cleanup Program application was accepted with no further action, opening Brownfields tax credit opportunities, per the application.

The market study shows a 15.9% overall capture rate (39.2% at 60% AMI) and 29 tax credit properties in the market area; the analyst flagged units smaller than comparables and a high share of three-bedroom units.

Council member Torres of District 3 supported the project, and Archway met with West Denver Renaissance Collaborative, Servicios de la Raza, Lifespan Local and the Denver Indian Center, per the application.
The application had planned a financing close in the second quarter of 2025; the groundbreaking came in 2026.

timeline.event: Land deeded to ULC CLT, LLC; Sheridan Homes takes the improvements with a Denver HOME loan
Archway Jody Acquisition LLC buys the Jody Apartments improvements
City Council approves assignment of the HOME covenant to Archway (resolution 23-1673)
CHFA announces 2024 Round Two awards, including Creekside Flats
City Council adopts the $7.5M loan agreement (26-0178) and a right-of-way encroachment permit for ULC CLT (26-0212)

General contractor (Calcon priced the 2024 design) and building permit numbers.
